description: This episode explores Edwin Hubble's 1929 discovery that the universe is expanding, built on Henrietta Leavitt's period-luminosity law for Cepheid variables and revealing that galaxies recede at speeds proportional to their distance. It traces the journey from the Great Debate about spiral nebulae through the measurement of cosmic distances to the realization that Einstein's general relativity equations had predicted expansion all along. Essential listening for anyone interested in cosmology, the history of astronomy, or how a single graph revolutionized our understanding of the universe's size, age, and fate.
